sources.title: Baidu frontend interview transcript preserving the Promise.all task and array-oriented reference implementation
Answer Batch 0019 mechanically extracted repository-source packet
ECMAScript Language Specification: Promise.all and PerformPromiseAll
Deterministic Node.js validation against native Promise.all
Source-first isolated review for the Promise.all candidate

claims.text: The retained repository image transcript explicitly asks for a handwritten Promise.all and includes an array-length reference implementation using Promise.resolve, indexed result storage, a completion counter, early rejection, and an empty-array branch.

Supporting arbitrary synchronous iterables instead of only the repository reference's array-oriented form is a deliberate specification-completeness extension and is not presented as recovered prompt text.

The chosen implementation assimilates each input through Promise.resolve, preserves input iteration order in the result, fulfills empty input with an empty array, and rejects the aggregate when an input rejection is first observed.

The candidate is a standalone myPromiseAll function fixed to the native Promise constructor and Promise.resolve; it intentionally does not claim the constructor-generic static-method behavior specified for Promise.all via its this value.
Aggregate rejection does not cancel already-started input work, and the candidate maintains O(n) result/handler state while acting as an aggregator rather than a concurrency limiter.

The exact Node.js fixture passes 12 fixed cases and 2000 deterministic randomized mixed-input cases against native Promise.all, including non-array iterables, sparse arrays, thenables, rejection timing, iterator exceptions, and empty-input callback timing.

findings: The candidate remains bounded to the Promise.all source task and explicitly labels iterable support as an extension beyond the array-oriented repository reference.
The implementation and native Promise.all oracle agree across fixed and randomized mixed-input cases.
The answer explains indexed order preservation, Promise.resolve assimilation, empty-input handling, rejection settlement, non-cancellation, and implementation genericity boundaries.
No personal or production experience is fabricated.
Formal promotion remains blocked only by the required human-approval gate.
